newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Talks thin, crude lends support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Talks thin, crude lends support.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market was quiet on Friday with most traders staying on the sidelines searching for directions.
Caltex Singapore sold by tender 20,000 tonnes of 380-cst grade fuel oil at a premium of $1.50 per tonne to spot Singapore quotes to Singapore Petroleum Co, industry sources said.
The cargo was awarded on an inter-tank transfer basis for April 26-28 lifting, the sources said.
"The premium is higher than in previous months, which shows prices are pretty well supported," said one trader, noting premiums were lower than $1 per tonne in January and February.
Sentiment has been very slow since the beginning of the week but prices were well supported by crude values, traders said.
The last offer was heard at $93.50 per tonne for the 380-cst grade on Wednesday.
The 380-cst was traded at $92.50 per tonne last week.
Sentiment in the LSWR market was dampened further after Indonesia allocated an additional 700,000 barrels of LSWR for April loading, bringing the April total to 4.3 million barrels.
As demand remained poor from Japan, the main LSWR importer, traders expected prices to soon fall below $15 per barrel, compared with $15.50 per tonne offered eailier this week.
"I think Japanese companies will only start enquiries in June for the summer season between July and September," said a Japanese trader in Tokyo.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
